notable_absence.finding: THIS IS THE 'ABSTRACT PAGES YIELD ALMOST NOTHING' RESULT, IN ITS PUREST FORM - reported plainly rather than padded. The page is 1.5 KB, of which the frontmatter and two boilerplate site links are a third. Its entire body is four sentences: a restatement of the description, a one-sentence definition of what a function is, one dependency statement, and two 'for more information, see' links. Everything the ontology knows about Eventing - eventing:function's 22 recurrences, OnUpdate/OnDelete handlers, bindings, the lifecycle-state scheme, timers, the advanced keyspace accessors, the self-recursion option - came from cloud/eventing/ example handlers and Capella reference pages, and NONE of it is here. The page that is architecturally the definition of the Eventing Service contributes 3 substantive relations and 1 new concept to a service that already has 12 registry concepts and 6 dedicated predicates. Specifically absent: no architecture section (contrast search-service.md, which has two diagrams and a scatter-gather description), no scaling or node-count guidance, no memory-quota note, no RBAC (not even a pointer to role:eventing-full-admin, which the registry already holds), no version or edition gate, no ports, no mention that Eventing is Enterprise-only if it is. There is no way to answer 'how does the Eventing Service work' from this page. The finding is not that extraction failed here; it is that this page carries less information than its own one-line description implies, and a reader arriving from services.md learns only that Eventing needs the Data Service.

cross_component_finding: SAME-WORD COLLISION, NEWLY CREATED BY THIS PAGE: 'Event'. The registry already holds monitoring:event ('a logged occurrence, subject of triggersAlert; scoped by monitoring:event-severity-enum (Info/Warning/Critical)') from the Capella monitoring batch. The Eventing Service's 'event' is a completely different thing - a trigger condition (a KV mutation or a timer firing) that causes user code to execute, with no severity, no tag, and no alerting. I have minted eventing:event separately and am flagging it rather than reusing monitoring:event; this is the same pattern as the ontology's existing four-way 'role' collision and its capella:cluster-manager / capella-role:cluster-manager pair. Note the irony that the service literally named after events is the one whose 'event' concept had to be minted last. Second observation for reconciliation: this page is the parent definition of eventing:function, yet the concept was minted from a child example page rounds earlier - the extraction order was leaf-first, and the leaf pages turned out to be far richer than the root. If the promotion rule is 'recurs on two or more distinct pages', that rule has been finding real Eventing structure entirely from examples, and this page's arrival changes nothing. That is evidence the two-or-more rule is robust to which page you happen to read first, but also that the conceptual tree is not where the vocabulary lives.
cross_product_finding: DEPLOYMENT-MODEL COMPARISON, EVENTING: the self-managed conceptual page and the Capella pages do not describe the same thing at different levels of detail - they describe disjoint aspects, and here the self-managed one is the poorer of the two. Capella's cloud/eventing/ tree (67 pages in round 8) produced the whole functional vocabulary: eventing:function, on-update-handler, on-delete-handler, binding/bucket-alias-binding/url-alias-binding, function-lifecycle-state, timer, curl-function, n1ql-function-call, advanced-keyspace-accessor, self-recursion-option. This page produces exactly one thing Capella's tree does not: the Data-Service co-deployment requirement, which Capella cannot state because Capella users do not choose which services run. So for Eventing the answer to 'does the service look like a different thing depending on deployment model' is: on Capella it looks like a JavaScript programming model, and on self-managed it looks like a cluster service you must remember to deploy alongside the Data Service - and neither description overlaps the other at all. There is no contradiction between them, but there is also no page anywhere in the corpus that presents both halves together. Also worth flagging for the docs, not just the ontology: privilege:capella-advanced-access-eventing-manage (registry, from cluster-rbac.md) is the only access-control fact the corpus holds about Eventing, and it is Capella-only; the self-managed access story for Eventing is represented in the registry solely by role:eventing-full-admin, which was found on a troubleshooting page, not here.
